question: Mia is “helping” her mom pick up \(30\) toys that are strewn on the floor. Mia’s mom manages to put \(3\) toys into the toy box every \(30\) seconds, but each time immediately after those \(30\) seconds have elapsed, Mia takes \(2\) toys out of the box. How much time, in minutes, will it take Mia and her mom to put all \(30\) toys into the box for the first time?
solution:
Track the number of toys just after Mom finishes each 30-second interval, before Mia removes any. After the first interval, this count is \(3\).

Between successive such moments, Mia removes \(2\) toys and Mom puts in \(3\), so the count increases by \(3-2=1\). The counts are therefore \(3,4,5,\ldots,30\). Reaching \(30\) requires \(30-3=27\) additional intervals, for a total of
\[
1+27=28
\]
intervals. Since each interval is half a minute, the time is
\[
28\cdot\frac12=14\text{ minutes}.
\]
All toys are in the box at that moment, before Mia's next removal. The answer is \(\boxed{14}\) minutes, choice B.
